title: OKR Initiative Decomposition & Ops Ramp for Company-wide Rollout
creator: Lina Patel
description:
Objective: Translate company-level OKRs into a concrete set of cross-functional initiatives with clear owners, success metrics, dependencies, and a repeatable cadence for kickoff, review, and course-correction.

Scope: Q4 company OKRs (Revenue Expansion, Reliability & SLOs, Developer Experience, and Deployments/Private). Deliverables include an initiative matrix (owner, squad, milestone map), a lightweight initiative template for squads to complete, a dependencies tracking board in Linear, and a public rollout calendar + kickoff emails.

Why: Past cycles showed uneven decomposition — some squads received high-level OKRs without owned initiatives or measurable signals. This ticket ensures consistent decomposition and operational cadence so leadership can monitor progress and unblock teams early.
acceptance_criteria: All company OKRs decomposed into no more than 3 initiatives each with a named owner and primary squad
Each initiative has 2–3 success metrics with data source and current baseline documented
Dependencies captured in Linear and linked to owning tickets (ENG/DES keys) for all initiatives
Kickoff sessions scheduled with Eng, Design, SRE, and Sales for each initiative within two weeks of rollup
Dashboard (Notion + Console shortlink) created showing progress and metric deltas for executive weekly reviews
Communication templates (email + Slack) prepared for initial rollout and biweekly updates
rollout_plan: 2025-10-02 to 2025-10-09: Run 3 decomposition workshops (Leadership, Eng Tech Leads, Design Leads)
2025-10-10 to 2025-10-16: Owners fill initiative templates; PM team validates metrics and baselines
2025-10-17: Publish initiative matrix and schedule kickoff meetings
2025-10-20 to 2025-11-03: Team kickoffs + dependency alignment; create Linear child issues for each dependency
2025-11-05: Executive weekly review dashboard goes live; first weekly status update due
2025-11-30: End-of-month checkpoint and retro; adjustments for next cycle
links: Google Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xExamplePRD (example PRDs and comms templates)
comments: 2025-10-01 — Lina Patel: Ticket created after exec planning sync. Priority set to P1 to ensure PM resources for decomposition workshops.
2025-10-04 — Marco Ruiz: Workshop 1 completed with Eng leads. Key decision: limit initiatives per OKR to 3 to keep focus; noted SRE capacity constraint for Reliability initiative.
2025-10-07 — Priya Nair (EM): Requested that success metrics include cost per inference for relevant initiatives; added ENG-3910 as dependency for metrics instrumentation.
2025-10-10 — Diego Morales (Design): Design lead approves initiative templates but requests an example filled template for Developer Experience; assigned DES-214 for design PRD.
2025-10-12 — Marco Ruiz: Draft initiative matrix published to Notion; flagged 2 high-risk dependencies (ENG-4122, Private Networking effort) and scheduled alignment calls.
2025-10-14 — Lina Patel: Drafted executive weekly review cadence and dashboard layout. Action: operationalize a short status form (2 fields: % complete, blockers) for weekly syncs.
notes: Trade-off: Depth vs speed — we'll accept lower metric completeness for 20% of initiatives this cycle to prioritize owner alignment and unblock kickoffs.
Decision: Use Linear as source-of-truth for dependencies to avoid divergent tracking spreadsheets.
Risk: SRE capacity during November may push Reliability initiative deliverables; plan to negotiate scoped canary for rollout if needed.
Follow-up: Schedule a 'metrics instrumentation' spike with Data infra (ENG-4205) to standardize telemetry for success metrics.
